stories.title: Majority of South Koreans not on board with US policy, first time in two decades — poll
stories.summary: In 2025, only 39% of respondents had a negative opinion about US policy while 61% of respondents held the opposite view
article_sentences: For the first time in 23 years, a majority (55%) of residents of the Republic of Korea negatively assess the policies of the United States, according to the results of a poll conducted by the US-based Pew Research Center.
The Center polled 1,045 people between March 3 and April 4, prior to US President Donald Trump ordering the Pentagon to scale back annual joint military exercises with South Korea.
"For the first time in over 20 years, a majority of South Koreans have an unfavorable opinion of the US," a report from the research center reads.
According to the data provided, a similar situation was recorded only in 2003 when 50% of respondents reported feeling negative towards the United States while 46% were pro-American.
The Center has been conducting research on this issue since 2002.
"South Koreans are much less likely than a few years ago to view the US as a reliable partner to their country," according to the report.
"While around six-in-ten South Korean adults (57%) consider the US a reliable partner, that’s down from 83% in 2022, when we last asked this question during the Biden administration."
In 2026, only 47% of respondents agreed that the United States contributes to peace and stability on the planet.
"A broad majority of South Koreans (85%) disapprove of the way Trump is dealing with tariffs, including 63% who strongly disapprove.
Only 14% approve of the US president’s handling of tariffs," the report continued.

stories.title: Iranian president expects to meet with Putin at SCO summit
stories.summary: The summit will be held in Bishkek on August 31 and September 1
article_sentences: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is expecting a meeting with Russian leader Vladimir Putin at the summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in Bishkek, according to Iranian TV channel Press TV.
According to it, Pezeshkian will take part in the summit, which will be held in the capital of Kyrgyzstan on August 31 and September 1.
The office of the head of the Iranian government has not yet officially commented on this information.

stories.summary: Neil Gilson completes 230-mile challenge after a ‘tough’ 22-hour crossing of Lac Léman He staggered rather than sprang out of the lake but it wasn’t surprising. Neil Gilson , a former international athlete, could be forgiven for feeling a little wobbly, having become the first person to swim the 10 largest lakes in Switzerland, a total of about 230 miles (370km).
